books.title: A Connecticut Yankee in King Arthur's Court
books.author: Mark Twain
books.desc: A practical nineteenth-century Yankee wakes up in King Arthur's England and sets out to modernise Camelot, with gunpowder, newspapers and plenty of trouble.
about: Hank Morgan, a head superintendent at an arms factory in Hartford, Connecticut, is knocked unconscious in a fight and wakes up in England in the year 528, at the court of King Arthur. Captured and condemned to be burned, he remembers that a solar eclipse is due and passes himself off as a great magician, rivalling Merlin. Soon he is "The Boss", the king's chief minister, determined to bring the inventions and ideas of his own century to the age of chivalry.

Twain mixes slapstick comedy and fantasy with biting satire of monarchy, aristocracy, the established Church, slavery and superstition. As Hank travels the land with the talkative Sandy and the king himself in disguise, the book raises serious questions about progress, power and the dangers of technology.
A Connecticut Yankee in King Arthur's Court was published in 1889. It is often cited as one of the early classics of time-travel fiction.

books.title: Babbitt
books.author: Sinclair Lewis
books.desc: George F. Babbitt, a prosperous real-estate man in the booming city of Zenith, has everything he is supposed to want, and begins to wonder why he is not happy.
about: George F. Babbitt is a successful real-estate broker in Zenith, a growing Midwestern city. He believes in business, boosters' clubs, modern gadgets and doing what his neighbours do, and his days are filled with deals, dinners, speeches and worries about status. Only with his old friend Paul Riesling does he admit to a vague dissatisfaction, until events shake his comfortable routine and he tries, for a while, to rebel.

Lewis satirises the conformity, materialism and boosterism of American middle-class life after the First World War with a sharp ear for slang and speeches, while making Babbitt a recognisable and at times sympathetic figure. The word "Babbitt" came to mean a self-satisfied, conformist businessman.
Babbitt was published in 1922, two years after Main Street. In 1930 Lewis became the first American to receive the Nobel Prize in Literature.

books.title: Daisy Miller
books.author: Henry James
books.desc: In Switzerland and Rome, a young American observes a pretty, free-spirited girl from New York whose disregard for European conventions scandalises society.
about: At a grand hotel in Vevey, Switzerland, Frederick Winterbourne, a young American who has lived long in Europe, meets Daisy Miller, a pretty, chatty girl from Schenectady travelling with her mother and her little brother Randolph. Charmed but puzzled, he cannot decide whether she is innocent or improper. When they meet again in Rome, Daisy's outings with a young Italian, Mr Giovanelli, scandalise the American expatriate community.
In this short and subtle novella, James contrasts American innocence and spontaneity with European manners and snobbery, and leaves readers, like Winterbourne, uncertain how to judge its heroine.
Daisy Miller first appeared in the Cornhill Magazine in June and July 1878 and in book form the following year. It brought James his first widespread critical and commercial success.

books.title: Herland
books.author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
books.desc: Three American explorers discover a hidden land inhabited only by women, and their assumptions about men, women and society are turned upside down.
about: Three young American men, the sociologist Van, who tells the story, the romantic Jeff and the swaggering Terry, hear rumours of a land where only women live, hidden on a plateau in an unexplored region. Flying in, they find a peaceful and orderly country with no men at all, where for two thousand years children have been born to women alone. Captured and gently educated by their hosts, including Ellador, Celis and Alima, the men must explain, and defend, the world they come from.

Gilman's feminist utopia uses humour and dialogue to question ideas about gender, motherhood, education and economics taken for granted in her time. Some of its assumptions, notably about race and selective breeding, reflect the eugenic thinking common in the early twentieth century.

Herland was serialised in 1915 in The Forerunner, the monthly magazine that Gilman wrote and edited herself. It was first published as a complete book only in 1979, and has since become a classic of feminist fiction.
books.author_short: American writer, lecturer and feminist (1860–1935), author of The Yellow Wallpaper, Women and Economics and Herland.
author_long: Charlotte Perkins Gilman was born in Hartford, Connecticut, on 3 July 1860. She became a leading writer, lecturer and theorist of the women's movement, arguing that women's economic independence was essential to the progress of society. From 1909 to 1916 she wrote and edited her own magazine, The Forerunner. She died in Pasadena, California, on 17 August 1935.

She is best known for the short story "The Yellow Wall-Paper" (1892) and the study Women and Economics (1898). Her many other works include novels such as Herland (1915), short stories, poems and thousands of essays.

books.title: Rebecca of Sunnybrook Farm
books.author: Kate Douglas Wiggin
books.desc: Imaginative, talkative Rebecca leaves her family's farm to live with two very different spinster aunts in a small Maine town, and brightens everyone's life.
about: Ten-year-old Rebecca Rowena Randall, one of seven children on the poor Sunnybrook Farm, is sent to live with her mother's older sisters in their brick house in Riverboro, Maine, so that she can be educated. Aunt Jane is gentle and kind, but Aunt Miranda is stern and quick to disapprove of Rebecca's chatter, daydreams and high spirits.

The novel follows Rebecca through school, friendships, small adventures and mishaps as she grows into a thoughtful and gifted young woman, helped along by a kind young businessman, Adam Ladd. It is a warm, humorous portrait of childhood and village life in New England.
Rebecca of Sunnybrook Farm was published in 1903 and became a lasting classic of American children's literature. It was adapted for the screen, including a 1917 film.
books.author_short: American educator and writer (1856–1923), pioneer of free kindergartens and author of Rebecca of Sunnybrook Farm.
author_long: Kate Douglas Wiggin was born in Philadelphia on 28 September 1856. In 1878 she opened the first free kindergarten in San Francisco, the Silver Street Free Kindergarten, and she became a leader of the kindergarten movement in the United States. She died on 24 August 1923 at Harrow, in England.
Alongside her work in education she wrote many stories and novels for children and adults, of which Rebecca of Sunnybrook Farm (1903) is the best known.
